name: Dark Synth Sci-Fi
brief: A cold, machine-made score. An analogue-style drone sits under everything and slowly opens and closes with a ladder-style low-pass filter. A sequenced arpeggio runs over it, pitched in phrygian or harmonic minor, and a pulsing bass locks to the grid. Industrial percussion, metallic hits and short noise bursts replace a drum kit, and a thin layer of additive air gives the top end a glassy sheen. The motion is in the filter and the arpeggio, not in a melody. Tempo 70 to 110, default 92. Prefer the Atelier engines for the drone, arpeggio and air when they are installed; native voices are the fallback.
neverDo: Quote or paraphrase a known synth-score theme or its arpeggio.
Keep the filter fixed; it must move across the cue.
Let the arpeggio play at one level; vary its gate, accent or octave.
Add a lead melody that hides the drone and the arpeggio.
Bundle a GPL or proprietary synth binary or a third-party factory preset.

bass.approach: A pulse bass on steady eighth notes, tightly gated, shifting root with the chord and dropping an octave at the cadence.

voicings: Open fifth drone on the root
Arpeggio on root, minor third, fifth and flat sixth
Additive air in the upper partials over the chord

habits: Start with the drone only, filter nearly closed.
Bring in the arpeggio, then open the filter over eight bars.
Add the pulse bass and industrial hits, then strip back to drone and air.
Close the filter again on the final phrase.

listeningNotes: A sustained drone is present throughout, and its brightness changes over time.
A sequenced arpeggio in phrygian or harmonic minor runs for most of the cue.
Filter movement shows as a rise and fall in the spectral centroid.
Pulse bass and industrial hits enter in the middle and leave before the end.
No lead melody covers the drone and the arpeggio.
